subject: Discovery recap: model-fit hypotheses, parity acceptance criteria & trial scope
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@fluxbank.com>, Tom Becker <t.becker@fluxbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: model-fit hypotheses, parity acceptance criteria & trial scope

Elena / Tom — thanks again for your time today. Quick call recap and proposed next steps so we can get a short evaluation trial scoped and started.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: triage + account summarization for inbound support tickets (prioritization + suggested responses).
- Current proprietary baseline: AcmeChat-prop-v2 (internal metric: 92% intent accuracy on historical labeled set; p95 response latency ~380ms).
- Main concerns: hallucinations in factual summarization, latency for synchronous UI, and cost per 1k requests.

Model-fit hypotheses (what to test in trial):
1) An appropriately tuned open candidate (LlamaX-13B-QR quantized) can match task-level intent accuracy within ~3 percentage points of your baseline while reducing inference cost by ~30%.
2) A smaller instruction-tuned open model (Mistral-7B-Instruct-quant) with prompt engineering and prefix caching will hit parity on F1 for entity extraction with lower latency at p95.
3) Hallucination reductions will primarily come from calibrated prompting + grounded retrieval rather than model size alone; therefore test both with/without retrieval.

Suggested acceptance criteria (parity gates):
- Intent accuracy on labeled dev set: within -3% of baseline or better.
- Entity F1: within -3 points of baseline.
- Hallucination rate (defined per eval plan): <= baseline + 2 percentage points.
- p95 latency: <= 350ms (for sync UI flows) with our suggested batch/merging strategy.

Proposed trial scope & artifacts we will provide:
- 2-week trial with 3 model variants: LlamaX-13B-QR (quant), Mistral-7B-Instruct-quant, Redwood-optimized-small (internal baseline simulating AcmeChat behavior).
- Prompt bundle (attached): 60 representative prompts + edge-case perturbations covering your ticket types. [attachment: prompt_bundle_fluxbank_v1.txt (text/plain)]
- Eval plan spreadsheet with metrics, thresholds, and runner instructions. [attachment: eval_plan_fluxbank_baseline.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
- Link to shared Drive with sample labels & runner: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fluxbank_eval

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm the labeled dev set (or share a small sanitized sample, ~500 tickets) so we can run initial baseline comparisons.
- Procurement contact to sign a short trial agreement (DocuSign link below once you confirm).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a 500-ticket sanitized sample this week (or we can use a synthetic subset).
2) We spin up trial infra (hosted trial or dedicated short-term pool) and run the eval harness against your baseline.
3) 5-day internal smoke test; then full 2-week trial with dashboards and weekly check-ins.

DocuSign for MSA (trial addendum) will be sent when procurement confirms — I'll loop Marissa to help with contracting and trial provisioning.

Attachments: prompt_bundle_fluxbank_v1.txt, eval_plan_fluxbank_baseline.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow if anything above needs to be adjusted.

—
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@fluxbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Becker <t.becker@fluxbank.com>, FluxBank Procurement <procurement@fluxbank.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model-fit hypotheses, parity acceptance criteria & trial scope

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we pull the sample: 

1) Data handling / compliance: we need to confirm SOC2 + data residency for the trial. Can you attach the SOC2 summary and the trial data retention policy?
2) When you say "baseline" (AcmeChat-prop-v2) can you share the exact metric definition you used for "intent accuracy" and the script to reproduce it? We want apples-to-apples runs.
3) Cost: can you provide a rough estimate (ballpark) for the two-week trial (hosted) including expected token counts? We need a number for procurement.

Also please confirm the p95 latency target — 350ms is our soft target, but 300ms would be preferable for UI responsiveness. If the open models need more aggressive quantization, we need to understand the anticipated quality delta.

If you can send SOC2 and a quick cost estimate today we can route to procurement and get the DocuSign out.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Customer Operations | FluxBank
elena.cruz@fluxbank.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@fluxbank.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model-fit hypotheses, parity acceptance criteria & trial scope (internal notes)

Karthik / Marissa — a couple of pragmatic suggestions I want us to include before we send cost numbers back to FluxBank: 

- Evaluation harness: use the fluxbank branch of our eval-harness (link below) and include the following test suites: intent_accuracy_v2 (label match with thresholding), entity_f1, hallucination_detector_v1 (grounded vs ungrounded output diff), and latency_p95. I pushed a config for batch_size and kv-cache settings that mimic their expected sequence lengths.
  https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/fluxbank

- Prompt perturbation sets: we should include a set of syntactic/semantic perturbations (typos, truncated context, injected noise) — these tend to expose hallucination regressions in instruction-tuned models. I've attached a short list in the eval plan. [attachment: eval_plan_fluxbank_baseline.xlsx]

- Parity gates (proposal):
  * Intent accuracy: >= baseline - 3% (strict)
  * Entity F1: >= baseline - 3 points
  * Hallucination rate: <= baseline + 2 points (measured by hallucination_detector_v1)
  * Latency p95: <= 330ms for hosted trial (we can aim for 300ms on Dedicated)

- Cost estimate approach (high-level):
  * LlamaX-13B-QR (quant): expect ~30-40% lower per-token compute cost vs baseline depending on batch config. For a 2-week pilot (estimate 200k request tokens total) ballpark hosted cost: $3k–$5k.
  * Mistral-7B-Instruct (quant): ~50% lower compute cost; ballpark hosted cost: $2k–$3k.
  * Dedicated short pool (5 GPU-hours/day): fixed commitment option — usually better if they expect sustained traffic.

- Compliance: attaching SOC2 summary and trial data-retention notes so procurement can see. [attachment: soc2_summary_redwood.pdf]

I'll prepare the exact benchmark command lines and runner config in the repo; Marissa, can you take the lead on contract addendum once procurement confirms?

—Priyom
Applied ML | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@fluxbank.com>, Tom Becker <t.becker@fluxbank.com>, FluxBank Procurement <procurement@fluxbank.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model-fit hypotheses, parity acceptance criteria & trial scope

Elena — thanks for the quick questions and Priyom for the details. To keep momentum, proposed immediate actions: 

1) FluxBank shares the 500-ticket sanitized sample by EOD Wednesday (or we seed with synthetic data if you prefer).
2) Procurement — I'll send a short DocuSign trial addendum (two-week hosted pilot) today; please review and loop in legal.
3) Marissa will provision the trial and set up the trial dashboard (link will be posted to the Drive).

Marissa — can you provision a hosted trial with the three variant images Priyom listed and enable the eval-harness branch? ETA by EOD tomorrow would be great.

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/FLX-20270502-01
Trial dashboard (will be live after provisioning): https://app.redwood.ai/trials/FLX-20270502-01

If no objections I'll send the DocuSign now and we can get procurement moving.

Best,
Karthik
